summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge for Soony: analyze the supplier/ERP data drops, find where the launch plan hides shortfalls, and build and ship a product (Lighthouse) that detects, explains and acts on them, ready for the 12:45 hand-in.
summary.outcome: Found the hidden Collector's Edition shortfalls (art book overbooking, failed statue lot, sleeve revision conflict, game card offload), built and shipped the Lighthouse recheck-and-act product with role-based UI, 'How we got here' flow, routines, demo reset tooling, and moved the jury demo (lighthouse.stenglein.dev) to ada; a verdict-text role fix is committed locally and unpushed. The silent demo video was not produced.

repo: Portal API has only three endpoints (files list, single file, archive.zip) with no webhooks; new or replaced files must be detected by polling and comparing SHA-256 checksums, and files can be replaced under the same name.
Confidential challenge data lives in gitignored data/ and .env; .env.example is committed with an empty SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN.
scripts/demo.sh has save-story/story commands and an open mode (ASK_DEMO_OPEN=on ASK_DEMO_HOST=...) to reset the demo to a prepared state; the demo records emails only and has calls off.
Team workflow is in CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md; a Now line is claimed in PROGRESS.md before starting work.
Entire hooks only write a checkpoint when repo files change, and push checkpoint refs on git push.

Hosting: live (ask-soony.stenglein.dev, password, real email) and old demo run on the Mac; lighthouse.stenglein.dev runs on ada in ~/Jonas/StartMunichHack/lighthouse-host with its own Cloudflare tunnel lighthouse-ada. The ada copy is a snapshot needing rsync plus restart for code changes.
A second connector of the same Cloudflare tunnel would split traffic across machines, so ada needed its own tunnel and a DNS repoint.
Verdict text on Launch previously did not know the viewing role, so Maren saw her own name; the role is now passed in.
workflow: Run long recorders or builds carefully: building mid-recording changes pages in the take, and the recorder wrote frames only at the end, so stopping it early lost everything.
Interrupted tool calls often still completed their commits, so check git state after an interruption.
Verify visual changes by measuring pixels (icon vs text rows) rather than guessing nudges.
Use View Transitions for list add/remove animation; unsupported browsers fall back safely.
Ask before pushing; the user pushes themselves, and a rejected push was just a remote-ahead fast-forward.

friction: Restarting the Cloudflare tunnel took all hosts down for about a minute; the first Ctrl-C closed its tmux session.
The hand-in time shifted from 12:00 to 12:45, which the assistant only learned late.
The logo nudge went the wrong direction first and needed measurement.
Phone layout issues (auto-scroll to the list, compact flow identical to the details view, jumping approve button) took several iterations.
A false data-check warning about a lost column came from a header read with the wrong separator.
The demo needed repeated resets because test runs and recordings changed its state.
The user's push was rejected because Lucas had pushed a README commit.
